title: Recurrent Neural Network
description: Give your network memory across time.
content:
**Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)** is a type of neural network designed to handle sequential data by maintaining internal memory. Unlike feedforward neural networks, where data is processed in one direction, RNNs have loop-back connections that help keep previous context. Tasks where time dependencies are crucial spread from natural language processing  or speech recognition to time series analysis

> How an RNN processes a sequence:
> • Data is processed unit by unit, one at each time step.
> • Previous data is retained in the hidden layers.
> • At each time step, the model combines the input and the hidden state to produce an output and update the hidden state, so the previous context is considered.

> The primary challenge lies in both vanishing and exploding gradients: gradients vanish or explode as they are propagated back through many time steps.

**Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)** is a type of RNN architecture designed to overcome vanishing and exploding gradient problems and capture long-term dependencies in sequential data. It captures and retains information over longer periods or sequences and helps mitigate the vanishing gradient problem thanks to its structure.

> LSTM consists of:
> • Forget gates - decide what information to discard from the previous cell state.
> • Input gates - determine which new information is added to the cell state.
> • Output gates - determine what the next hidden state (and possibly the output) should be by regulating what information from the cell state is exposed to the next time step.
> • Cell state update - combines the retained past information and the new candidate to update the cell's memory.
